name: William Gibbes House

dates.altered: Redecorated in 1794, when the double staircase with its iron rail was added (the SC register).
dates.note: The SC register says 'built sometime shortly after 1772, and redecorated in 1794'; the Wikipedia infobox prints 1775; the HABS addendum for the Blacklock House cites it as 'the William Gibbes House (1772)'. Recorded as the state register states it; the exemplar's year is null because no source read gives a single year.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 70000575; added April 15, 1970; designated NHL April 15, 1970; contributing to the Charleston Historic District (ID66000964) (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it; the SC register prints the same two dates)
National Register Properties in South Carolina -- William Gibbes House, Charleston County (64 S. Battery, Charleston)
refs.note: 'one of the finest two-story frame residences in America ... built upon a high English basement of carefully distressed stone ... The modillions at the cornice level are carried around all sides of the building, and the building is roofed by a tiled hipped roof ... The Gibbes House has the usual Georgian four-room double pile floor plan, known in Charleston simply as a double house.'
